column3: Near-exact parallel: intercession benefits only one permitted by the Merciful, with approved speech added.
It is a nearby resurrection objection but does not clarify permission, intercession, or the released hearts.
It shows harm and benefit operating only by Allah's permission, without the intercession setting.
It joins a question about speech to hearts sealed against understanding, contrasting the focus's truth-bearing response.
The immediate context denies Iblis independent authority, framing the focus's denial of independent intercessory power.
It identifies truth as coming from the Lord, but lacks the focus's authorized speech and intercession setting.
It denies those invoked besides Allah ownership of intercession and ties the exception to truthful, knowing witness.
It describes arrogant hearts being sealed, only a secondary contrast to hearts cleared for truthful speech.
It closely states that even angels' intercession is ineffective until Allah permits and approves.
It closely parallels speech being permitted by the Merciful and constrained to what is right.
David's granted favor and softened iron do not materially develop either focal movement.
Its fearful hearts before return to their Lord loosely illuminate the focus's hearts after fear is removed.
It makes intercession unavailable except through a covenant with the Merciful.
The immediate context denies Iblis authority and affirms the Lord's guardianship over all things.
Hardened hearts and Satan's beautification contrast with hearts released into recognition of truth.
The same question about what the Lord sent receives the false answer "legends," contrasting the focus's answer, "the truth."
Allah's declaration that He speaks the truth directly reinforces the focus's verdict on what the Lord said.
It identifies Allah as the true protector, providing a broad frame for the focus's closing exaltation.
It directly asks who can intercede with Allah except by His permission within His complete knowledge and authority.
The command to David's household to give thanks does not clarify the focal themes.
It states that intercessors' intercession will not benefit them, supplying the negative boundary to the focus.
It assigns judgment to Allah the Most High, the Most Great while rejecting association with Him.
The immediately preceding verse denies alleged partners any ownership, share, or supporting role.
It explicitly denies the idolaters any intercessors from their alleged partners.
It repeats that Allah is the True, the Most High, the Most Great, directly echoing the focus's conclusion.
Faith is not compelled even under divine will; this only broadly relates to permission and response.
It links events and the heart's guidance to Allah's permission, without the focal intercession or speech scene.
It repeats that Allah is the True, the Most High, the Most Great and all rivals are false.
Saba's turning away and punishment belong to the local surah setting but do not develop the focal claim.
Believers recognize the Hour as truth while others dispute it, a broader recognition-of-truth parallel.
The condemned acknowledge the warning they received, but it does not address authorized intercession or speech.
The statement of divine favor and knowledge has no material connection to the focal movements.
It presents corroborated evidence as truth from the Lord, without the focus's permission structure.
The reminder's benefit to believers shares only the word-benefit dimension of the focus.
The same surah declares that truth has come and falsehood can neither originate nor restore anything.
The Lord's word becoming due against disbelievers is only a general truth-and-judgment connection.
Divine ownership and the titles Most High and Great provide the authority frame for the focus's ending.
It explicitly connects faith and the heart to Allah's permission, though not to intercession.
It states that harm cannot occur except by Allah's permission and directs believers to rely on Him.
Guidance and favor are assigned to Allah, but the sectarian speech context is remote from the focus.
It declares the Book beyond doubt and from the Lord of the worlds, supporting the source of the truthful word.
The oath by the even and odd is not an intercession reference and does not clarify the focus.
Fear, reassurance, judgment by truth, and guidance form a close narrative parallel to the focus's released hearts and true answer.
It directly states that no intercessor acts except after Allah's permission amid His governance of all affairs.
It names the message as truth from the Lord and forbids doubt, but adds no focal mechanism.
It assigns all intercession exclusively to Allah and grounds that claim in His dominion and final return.
It treats divine permission as necessary for assigning lawful status, a secondary authorization parallel.
The misuse of the language of right does not materially illuminate authorized intercession or divine speech.
Joseph's refusal to punish anyone but the responsible person has no substantive focal connection.
The decree to fill Hell with Satan and his followers does not develop the focus's themes.
The condemned people's lack of intercessors supplies the negative counterpart to permitted intercession.
Its weighing of harm against benefit is only a lexical and general evaluative parallel.
Hypocrites' self-justifying oaths after calamity do not clarify the focal relation.
Permission to join a later campaign is unrelated to the focus's divine authorization.
Covered hearts and calling revelation old tales sharply contrast with hearts freed to identify the Lord's speech as truth.
Speaking a penetrating word to those whose hearts Allah knows is a limited speech-and-heart parallel.
It rebukes failure to measure Allah rightly and affirms His strength and might, broadly supporting His exclusive authority.
The contrast of recompense for wrongdoers and believers does not develop the focal themes.
Obedience to difficult commands and resulting steadiness are not a material counterpart to the focus.
Abraham's sound heart loosely contrasts with hearts affected by fear in the focus.
It calls later revelation truth while exposing selective belief, but lacks the focus's authorization or speech scene.
It calls the revelation truth from the Lord against the charge of fabrication, a general speech-truth parallel.
It contrasts truth with falsehood and identifies what benefits people as what remains, joining both focal terms conceptually.
The same surah's scene of sudden fear and capture gives an eschatological contrast to the focus's fear being removed.
The messenger is obeyed only by Allah's permission, and his prayer accompanies repentance, a bounded mediation parallel.
It describes disputing with falsehood to dislodge truth, directly contrasting the focus's recognition of truth.
Hearts with disease ask what Allah intended, while the verse distinguishes guidance, certainty, and misguidance.
Satan's threat to wait on the straight path does not materially clarify the focus's intercession or speech scene.
It challenges the choice of intercessors that possess nothing and do not understand.
A public inquiry reaches a truthful answer through testimony and confession, closely paralleling truth disclosed in speech.
The commanded spoken plea for forgiveness is only a distant authorized-speech parallel.
Gabriel brings confirming guidance to the Prophet's heart by Allah's permission, but not in an intercession setting.
The prayer concerning Pharaoh's heart is a remote heart-and-divine-action parallel.
The false naming of angels does not clarify intercession, permission, or the focal exchange.
The messenger is sent with truth as bearer of good news and warning, but this does not develop the focal scene.
Diseased hearts and concealed motives are only a broad contrast to hearts released into truthful recognition.
Faith requires accepting the messenger's judgment without inner resistance, a bounded parallel to receptive hearts and true speech.
Allah's invitation to forgiveness by His permission is a remote authorization parallel.
Advancing in good deeds occurs by Allah's permission, but without the focus's intercession or speech context.
It explicitly says conjecture cannot avail against truth, sharpening the focus's answer that the Lord said the truth.
The granted permission for defensive fighting is a different, limited form of authorization.
Allah's exclusive knowledge of the Hour and hidden matters does not materially develop the focal themes.
Its declaration of the truth of certainty strongly reinforces the focus's identification of the divine word as truth.
It contrasts security from fear on that Day with the focus's fear being lifted, though in a different scene.
It denies accepted intercession and any substitute or help on the Day of judgment.
The angels' unwearied worship under Allah's ownership provides only a broad authority frame.
It closely parallels that no soul may speak on that Day except by Allah's permission.
The question of whether Salih is sent by his Lord has only a limited speech-and-recognition connection.
The question whether Abraham brought truth or play directly frames truth as the issue of a spoken claim.
The oppressed people's complaint and Moses's response do not materially clarify the focus.
The completed word concerning Hell is only a general divine-decree parallel.
It states that they will not be permitted to speak an excuse, the negative counterpart to permitted speech.
It prohibits remaining with mockery of Allah's verses, but does not directly develop the focus's speech or intercession.
The repeated qualification that Jesus's acts occur by Allah's permission directly denies independent delegated power.
The instruction to provide for dependents and speak kindly has no material focal connection.
Heedless hearts and secret speech that calls revelation magic contrast with the focus's hearts released to speak truth.
A sign leads one person to certainty about Allah's power, a distant recognition-of-truth parallel.
It repeats the formula "truth of certainty," strongly reinforcing the focus's final truth claim.
The source of revelation in the Creator has no material connection to the focal mechanisms.
Accumulated deeds rust hearts, providing a contrast to hearts relieved of fear and able to recognize truth.
It denies that intercession will be accepted on the Day when no soul can avail another, supplying the focus's negative boundary.
It treats intercession as a consequential act for good or evil, a human-level counterpart to the focus's strict divine authorization.
It warns that those gathered to their Lord will have no protector or intercessor besides Him.
It exposes alleged partner-intercessors as absent when people return to Allah alone.
The condemned ask whether intercessors can intercede for them, placing intercession in the irreversible judgment scene.
It rejects invoking supposed intercessors besides Allah and exposes the claim that they intercede with Him.
The same question about what the Lord sent receives the answer "good," closely paralleling the focus's question-and-true-answer exchange.
The angels intercede only for those Allah approves and stand in awe before Him, directly limiting intercession to divine approval.
It denies any protector or intercessor besides Allah after affirming His creation and governance.
It rejects lesser gods whose intercession would not avail at all if the Merciful intended harm.
It states that wrongdoers will have neither devoted friend nor an intercessor whose plea is obeyed.
It limits direct divine speech to specified modes and closes by naming Allah the Most High, joining authorization and divine communication.
It describes the Day when they will not speak, immediately framing the later statement that they are not permitted to excuse themselves.
It declares Allah's word to be truth and places final dominion on the Day the Trumpet is blown.
It declares the Lord's word complete in truth and justice, reinforcing the focus's verdict that what the Lord said is truth.
It announces that truth has come and falsehood has vanished, closely complementing the same-surah declaration in 34:49.
